pattern: Catalogue vs inventory: separate the description of a thing (title, ISBN) from its physical instances (copies with barcodes and status); model each lending event as its own object (loan, reservation) and keep business rules (limits, fines) and notifications behind interfaces.

tips.nudge: What is the library's main job for a member?
tips.hint: Write a requirement for taking a copy home.
tips.show: F1: A member borrows an available copy; the loan is due in 14 days.

tips.nudge: The book has to come back.
tips.hint: Add a requirement for returning a copy and what happens then.
tips.show: F2: Returning a copy closes the loan, charges a fine if late, and offers the copy to the next reservation.

tips.nudge: How does a member know whether the library has a book?
tips.hint: Add a requirement for finding titles.
tips.show: F3: Members search the catalogue by title, author or subject and see how many copies are available.

tips.nudge: Can a member take 200 books for a year?
tips.hint: State the limits, the loan period and what happens when it is exceeded.
tips.show: F4: At most 5 items per member, 14-day loans renewable once if nobody waits, a fine per day late.

tips.nudge: Every copy is out. Does the member just leave?
tips.hint: Add a requirement for joining a line and being told when a copy is back.
tips.show: F5: Members reserve a title; on return the first in line is notified and has 3 days to collect.

tips.nudge: Which method does the desk call when a member takes a copy?
tips.hint: An operation taking a member and a copy and returning the loan.

tips.nudge: Which method does the returns slot call?
tips.hint: An operation taking the copy's barcode.

tips.nudge: Three people borrowed the same novel. Is that one object or three?
tips.hint: Separate what describes a title from what sits on the shelf.
tips.show: Book(isbn, title, authors, subjects) has many BookCopy(barcode, status, location).

tips.nudge: Where does the due date live?
tips.hint: Model each borrowing event as its own object.
tips.show: Loan(id, member, copy, borrowed_at, due_at, returned_at?, renewals).

tips.hint: Add a class for the person who borrows.
tips.show: class Member { id, name, active_loans, fines_owed; can_borrow() }

checks.label: Physical item is a first-class object

tips.nudge: Is there a box on your diagram for the thing with the barcode?
tips.hint: Add a class for a single physical copy with its status.
tips.show: class BookCopy { barcode, status: CopyStatus } with Book 1 → * BookCopy.

checks.label: Changeable rules sit behind an abstraction

tips.nudge: The library changes its fine rules next month. Which classes change?
tips.hint: Have the lending service depend on interfaces for rules and notifications.
tips.show: Library uses FinePolicy (PerDayFine, CappedFine) and Notifier (EmailNotifier, SmsNotifier).

tips.nudge: Children's books have no fine, adult books have a cap. Where do those rules live?
tips.hint: Compare computing the fine inside Loan with a separate policy object.
tips.show: FinePolicy strategy chosen per item type; Loan only knows its dates; new rules are new policy classes.

checks.label: How waiting members hear about a return

tips.nudge: Return code should not know about email, SMS and push.
tips.hint: Compare calling an email client directly with raising an event that listeners handle.
tips.show: Observer: return_copy raises CopyAvailable; the ReservationQueue moves the copy to ON_HOLD and a Notifier interface tells the first member.

tips.nudge: Two desks scan the last copy of a bestseller in the same second.
tips.hint: Say how a copy is claimed atomically and how the model grows (new item types, more branches).
tips.show: Claim a copy with a compare-and-set on its status (or a per-copy lock / DB row lock); member limit checked inside the same transaction. New media (DVD) = a new Item subclass; branches = a location on the copy.

tips.nudge: Have you written the title, the copy, the member, the loan and the lending method?
tips.hint: Declare the domain classes and the lending service with its checkout method.
tips.show: class Book, BookCopy, Member, Loan; class Library: checkout(member_id, barcode) -> Loan; return_copy(barcode).
